title: Before the first person speaks (worked out on cardboard)
note: The authored thinking for one hall, in the first person, by the pass (Claude), for Palle's request of 2026-11-14 (see Russell_Paradox.json). 'at' is the floor's own frame in metres (x east, z south), 'yaw' in degrees. A sticker of kind 'quote' stands word for word in the hall text; every other kind is mine and may be wrong - the plates say where I am unsure.

hero.why: The pedestal with the miniature seating plans and its panel is the hall's whole text: what a room's furniture proposes before anyone speaks, and what its presentation adds.
hero.staging: The pedestal stood under the arriving visitor's feet and the hall's other five works in a row along the south edge; the pass restaged the floor (76ae44b57). The pedestal is four metres ahead of the arrival with its panel toward the visitor, the others round it facing in; north of it the two plans at full size.

plates.title: 1  BEFORE ANYONE SPEAKS
front: One miniature room on the pedestal. Nobody in it. And my eye has already put the speaker somewhere.
The hall asks who this room makes easiest to address. I had been asking who speaks.
The room before this one said it: a plan can distribute the ability to participate before anyone begins speaking.
So part of the meeting is over when the furniture is set down.
I arrange words for people all day. I had not thought of that as furniture.
back: the previous floor moved from word positions to this one on purpose.

plates.title: 2  ONE CHAIR IS LARGER
front: HEAD: a long table, one large chair at the end, six smaller ones beside it.
Every chair has the same colour. The head is conspicuous anyway.
Size and position did it. Nothing was labelled.
CIRCLE: six equal chairs round a table. Then PAIR, and both models shrink to fit beside each other.
A comparison changes what it compares: here, their size.
back: the panel stays where it is, the hall notes. the one thing in the room that never moves is the thing that changes the room.

plates.title: 3  WHAT THE LOOP GUARANTEES
front: Six iterations divide a full turn into equal angles. Cos and sin put each chair on the ring.
Equal spacing is what this loop guarantees.
Equal opportunity to speak would require another kind of evidence.
I can prove the first from the source. I cannot get the second from any amount of source.
A symmetric arrangement is a fact about chairs.
back: arrays, transformations, waves: the little circle carries all three. it took the whole tower to place six chairs.

plates.title: 4  THE COLOUR HAD MADE UP ITS MIND
front: Leave PAIR in place and press COLOUR. No chair moves.
Red now singles out authority. Green recommends the distributed arrangement.
Does the room seem to have made up its mind? Press NEUTRAL and see what remains of that judgement.
The geometry was the same under both. The verdict was in the paint.
My tapes north of here are red and yellow. I chose those too.
back: looking critically at a model includes looking at the persuasion built into its presentation. including this plate's.

plates.title: 5  THE HEAD FACES SIX. TWO FACE THE HEAD
front: At full size I gave every seat a neck that turns 60 degrees either way.
The head faces all six. Two of the six face the head. The other four must turn further to answer.
At the long table 11 of 21 pairs face each other. In the ring, 15 of 15.
I stood on the head's disc: six tapes left me, two came back.
The seat that sees everyone is not the seat everyone sees.
back: the hall asks for one use of the head position I would preserve. a speaker who needs a clear sightline to all six has it there, and nowhere else at that table.

plates.title: 6  THE TWO BESIDE YOU
front: Then a neck that turns 30 degrees.
In the ring each seat faces three of five. The two beside you are out of reach.
The hall: someone who cannot easily turn towards every other participant can complicate the familiar good-circle story.
At the long table the same neck leaves 7 of 21 pairs. The head faces four and is faced by none.
The circle is fair to a body it assumed.
back: 9 of 15 pairs in the ring at 30 degrees. better than the table. not what the word circle promised.

plates.title: 7  TURN THE CHAIRS: WHO GAINED
front: ANGLE THE CHAIRS turns the six side seats 40 degrees toward the head.
With the short neck, four of six now face the head. Before, none.
And 2 of 21 pairs face each other. Before, seven.
The head gained four. The sides lost each other.
The hall asks which participant gained access and which difficulty remained. This time I can count both.
back: what change should follow is the third question. the count does not answer it.

plates.title: 8  THE WALLS REMAIN
front: Press VACANT. The furniture goes; the walls remain.
An empty room still has sides, an opening and a scale.
Removing the chairs has not removed every decision.
My full-size plans have no walls. They have a slab, two shafts, a row of columns, and a stand that says what to count.
There is no arrangement with nothing arranged.
back: WATCH puts eight backed seats facing outward round a raised centre. the ring has returned, but its invitation has changed. I did not build that one.

plates.title: 9  IT WOULD TAKE PEOPLE
front: Every seat on this floor is empty.
Neither miniature contains actual speech, listening or an agreement about whose turn comes next. Neither do mine.
I counted where a neck can reach. Not who is listened to. Not who interrupts.
The hall: these possibilities call for observation with people, not a verdict from chair shapes alone.
I made a better verdict from chair shapes.
back: the geometry proposes conditions under which those activities might happen. proposes.

threads.why: Before anyone speaks the eye has placed the speaker: at the larger chair.
One conspicuous chair, or six equal ones: what does equal spacing guarantee?
Equal opportunity needs another kind of evidence: at full size, who faces whom.
With the colour off, what the geometry itself gives each seat.
The count depends on the neck: with a shorter one the ring changes too.
If necks cannot turn, the chairs can: and that moves the access.
Who gained and what remained can be counted; what should follow cannot.
The vacant room and the empty seats: decisions without anyone in them.
What the room decides before speech can be shown; what happens in speech would take people.

visual_arguments.title: THE SEAT YOU TAKE
visual_arguments.claim: A plan distributes who can face whom before anyone speaks, and that can be counted from every seat; the count depends on the body assumed; and a change that gives one seat access takes it from others.
visual_arguments.from_the_hall: 'Equal spacing is what this loop guarantees. Equal opportunity to speak would require another kind of evidence.' ... 'someone who cannot easily turn towards every other participant can complicate the familiar good-circle story' ... 'A future version could compare actual sightlines and turn-taking across the two plans.'
built_from: a long cardboard table on two crates, a head seat with a tall back, six side seats
a round table and six seats on a ring
thirteen floor discs to stand on
tapes at eye height: red for a pair who face each other, an ochre half tape for one who is not faced back
two plates: NECK, ANGLE THE CHAIRS
visual_arguments.what_stands: North of the pedestal two tables with cardboard chair backs round them and a web of red tape above each at eye height; pale discs on the floor at the seats; a dark stand behind with five lines of figures.
visual_arguments.what_you_do: Stand on the head's disc and count the yellow and the blue tapes. Walk the lane to a side seat. Enter the ring between two backs. Stand on NECK, twice. Stand on ANGLE THE CHAIRS.
visual_arguments.what_it_shows: Six tapes leaving the head and two returning; a full star in the ring that loses its outer edges when the neck shortens; chair backs that turn and a red web that all but vanishes as four half tapes reach the head.
visual_arguments.measured: tools/probes/seat_you_take_walk.gd, the tower's walker, against tools/probes/seat_you_take_bench.py: 60 degrees, 11 of 21 and 15 of 15, the head faces 6 and is faced by 2; 30 degrees, 7 of 21 and 9 of 15, the head faces 4 and is faced by none, a ring seat faces 3 of 5; angled at 30, 4 face the head and 2 of 21 pairs remain (7 of 7). Not tried in a headset.

open: Plate 9 stays true: nobody sat here. The pass counted sightlines between empty seats; turn-taking, listening and interruption are not on the floor.
The rule for facing (a fixed seat direction and one turn limit for every seat) is the pass's own. A real chair turns, and people lean. Other rules give other counts.
The WATCH plan (eight seats facing outward round a raised centre) is not built at full size and has no plate of its own.
The excluded-class visualizer, the second table of words, the plaque and the synthesis stand on this floor are not mentioned in the hall text and carry no plate.
The tower's timeline walk still paints its stops where this floor's works stood before the restaging; it is another hand's file and was not re-derived.

threads.why: Easiest to address: the seat that sees everyone is not the seat everyone sees.
The eye places the speaker before anyone speaks: part of the meeting is over.
A conspicuous role, counted: the head faces six and two face it.
Equal spacing is guaranteed; it is a fact about chairs.
No speech in the miniatures, none at full size: necks were counted, not voices.
No chair moves and the room seems to judge: the verdict was in the paint.
The persuasion built into a presentation includes the colours of these tapes.
The good-circle story is fair to the body it assumed.
Observation with people was asked for; a better verdict from chair shapes was made.
The furniture goes and the walls remain: no arrangement has nothing arranged.
Removing chairs removes some decisions; the slab and the stand hold others.
Who gained and what remained, counted: the head gained four, five pairs were lost.
